# javaabu/workflows

> Dynamic workflows for Laravel. A workflow is steps (start, task, decision, action, end) joined by transitions with labels, conditions and actions; tasks have assignees (the starter, users, roles, permissions, the subject's relations, earlier actors, custom types). Definitions are versioned (drafts, immutable published versions; instances keep theirs), defined fluently in seeders (Workflows::define()->steps([...])->transitions([...])->sync()), in a keyboard-accessible drag-and-drop builder (React, in Inertia and mounted in Blade), or by an optional laravel/ai assistant. Instances keep their data, tasks and history, and fire events. Steps collect data with javaabu/form-builder forms. Actions: notify (javaabu/notifications when installed), update_model, set_data, webhook, and your own. A tester simulates runs with sample data. Pages in Blade and Inertia React (Route::workflows(), Route::workflowTasks()), permissions through javaabu/permissions, optional javaabu/translatable. English and Dhivehi, RTL.

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/workflows/.

## Rules

- Define code-owned workflows in a seeder with `Workflows::define('key')->for(Model::class)->steps([...])->transitions([...])->sync()`. `sync()` validates and is idempotent; `->locked()` keeps a workflow to code. Admins build others on `Route::workflows()` pages.
- Exactly one `Step::start()`, at least one `Step::end()`. Every step but an end needs a way out and a path to an end. Give every decision one transition without conditions (the default).
- Move instances only with `$model->startWorkflow()` / `Workflows::start()`, `$instance->transition($key, by: $user, data: $request, comment: …)` and `cancel()`. Never write `current_step`, `status` or `outcome`.
- Never change a published version: change the draft (`$workflow->draft()`, the builder, `sync()`), then `$workflow->publish()`. Instances stay on the version they started with; don't rename step keys on published workflows.
- Decide who acts with `$instance->canAct($user)` / the policy's `act`, and list inboxes with `WorkflowTask::query()->open()->assignedTo($user)`. Users are morphs: nothing assumes `App\Models\User` or the `web` guard; pass `guard` to the route macros.
- Text (names, labels, notification text) is a string or a locale map `['en' => …, 'dv' => …]`: read it with `Workflows::text()`.
- Collect step data with form-builder forms (`->form('key')`); use `->skipForm()` on transitions like Reject. Conditions read `days`, `subject.amount`, `starter.name`.
- Put workflow side effects in actions (`->runs('notify', [...])`), custom ones extending `Javaabu\Workflows\Actions\Action` registered with `Workflows::registerAction()`; implement `ShouldQueue` for slow ones. Use the events for app-wide concerns.
- Register routes with `Route::workflows([...])` and `Route::workflowTasks([...])` inside the `web` group, and run `php artisan permissions:sync`. Override controllers from `config('workflows.controllers')` and policies with `Gate::policy()`.
- Test paths with `Workflows::simulate()`, side effects with Laravel's fakes, the assistant with `WorkflowAssistantAgent::fake()`. Use Thaana in tests of user-facing behaviour, and logical CSS in views.
